fields.title: Remove implicit state machines from the Runlimit crates
fields.description:
## Outcome
Every implicit state machine in the five native Runlimit packages and the batter-runlimit adapter is either replaced by a type-level representation (type-state, consuming transition, exhaustive enum, sealed capability or library-owned ordering) or recorded, under ADR-010 review question 5, as application policy, upstream behaviour or inherent persisted state whose in-process decode is made exhaustive. On the canonical native and protected paths no caller has to remember an ordering, a paired call, non-emptiness, a transaction boundary or an outcome to keep a documented invariant.

## Scope and authority
Crates: runlimit-core, runlimit-memory, runlimit-postgres, runlimit-http, runlimit-axum and crates/batter-runlimit. This epic is the catalog and the cross-task decision record; it authorizes no code change, commit, publication or release by itself. Child tasks own delivery scope, acceptance, priority, status and blocker edges. Every native public item is consumer-facing through the facade reexports (batter::runlimit::native, ::memory, ::postgres, ::native_transport), so a public hard cut follows the AGENTS.md rule: a `Breaking:` CHANGELOG entry with before/after code per affected call shape (runlimit/CHANGELOG.md for native packages, root CHANGELOG.md where the facade surface changes), a `Migration:` rustdoc sentence naming the removed item, a recorded `#[deprecated]` shim decision, and a public-API surface diff. Never rewrite published migrations, advisory lock namespaces, shard derivation or subject-key derivation. No second limiter engine. Unix-only.

## Evidence
Static source audit at HEAD 986d294 on 2026-11-08. Every production source file in the six crates and every SQL file under runlimit/runlimit-postgres was read in full; the anchors cited by child tasks were re-read against the working tree. Starting point: repository inventory rows L01-L07 and H03/H04 in docs/evidence/implicit-state-machines-2026-11-05.md; H04 was remediated by batter-jnjj (commit 4639571) and its residue is catalogued here. The audit found 33 raw families: runlimit-core 5, runlimit-memory 9, runlimit-postgres 11, transport and adapter 8. Overlapping families were merged into the child tasks; the finding map and the rejected candidates are recorded in the first comment. No code, tests or live PostgreSQL were executed for the audit: representable-but-invalid states are source-confirmed, not runtime-reproduced, except where a task names an existing test.

## Classification used
Implicit: phase inferred from data (Option, bool, counter, timestamp, collection membership, SQL predicate). Mixed: an explicit state type exists but extra fields or control flow carry essential substates or transition obligations. Protocol: the sequence lives in the program counter and local ownership with no enduring phase value. Configuration, diagnostic counters, ordinary iteration and compiler-generated async state were excluded. A family is debt when a canonical consumer or a third-party backend can compile a known-invalid ordering, pairing, emptiness or omission that the library has enough information to prevent.

## Verification policy
Each task records its ADR-010 invalid-state review, adds the failure-path or `compile_fail` evidence that the removed state is unrepresentable, runs `bash scripts/verify.sh` on the pinned toolchain, runs the named live PostgreSQL tests where the task touches runlimit-postgres, and records actual outcomes in the task. Keep allocation counts on the memory hot path at or below today's (batter-jv92, batter-5618). Fresh-agent usability evaluations are proposals unless executed.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Every child task is closed, each either with a type-level representation that makes the catalogued invalid states unrepresentable and a failure-path or compile_fail test proving it, or with a recorded ADR-010 question-5 justification (application policy, upstream protocol, inherent persisted state with an exhaustive decode). No debug_assert!, expect or doc-only guard protects a phase assumption at any site catalogued here. Every public hard cut shipped with its Breaking: CHANGELOG entry, Migration: rustdoc, shim decision and public-API diff. runlimit/AGENTS.md and crates/batter-runlimit/AGENTS.md invariants name the enforcing type wherever a documented rule became a type rule. Full scripts/verify.sh passed on the delivered tree.
